lines.text: Good morning, and thank you for coming in. Please have a seat. Could you tell me a little about yourself?

Good morning, and thank you for having me. I am a Java developer with a strong interest in backend systems. Over the last year I have been building projects and solving data structure problems every day.
That sounds good. What kind of projects have you worked on?
Mostly small but complete applications. For example, I built an expense tracker with a REST API and a database, and I handled validation and error cases myself.
And what made you choose software development?
I enjoy solving problems, and I like that I can build something that people actually use. Every bug I fix teaches me something new.
How would you describe your technical skills at the moment?
My strongest area is core Java and object-oriented design. I am comfortable with Spring Boot, SQL and Git, and I am still improving my knowledge of testing and system design.
How do you keep your skills up to date?
I follow a daily routine. I solve one or two problems, read about one new concept, and build small features in my own projects. I also read other people's code on GitHub.
Have you worked in a team before, or mostly alone?
Mostly on college and personal projects, but a few of them were team projects. I learned to use Git branches, write clear commit messages and ask for reviews.
What is one thing you are proud of in your journey so far?
Learning everything step by step on my own. I did not have much guidance at the start, but I kept going, and now I can build a complete application from the database to the API.
What are you looking for in your next role?
I want to join a team where I can learn from experienced developers and take real responsibility for my work.

lines.text: What would you say is your biggest strength?
I would say it is consistency. When I start learning something, I practise it every day until I can use it confidently, and I do not give up when it gets difficult.
Can you give me an example?
Last year my English speaking was weak, so I practised speaking for thirty minutes daily. Within a few months I could join team discussions comfortably.
Interesting. And what is a weakness you are working on?
Sometimes I spend too long on one problem before asking for help. I am learning to set a time limit, and after that I ask a teammate.
Interesting. Can you tell me more about how you work on that weakness?
Yes. When I start a task, I note the time. If thirty minutes pass and I have no progress, I write down what I tried and ask a teammate. This also saves their time because my question is specific.
Do you have a strength that is useful specifically in a team?
I think it is being reliable. If I say I will finish something by Thursday, I tell the team early when there is a risk, so nobody is surprised.
How do you handle feedback when someone points out a mistake?
I try not to take it personally. I thank the person, fix the problem, and think about how to avoid it next time. Honestly, feedback is the fastest way for me to improve.
And how do you handle pressure near a deadline?
I break the work into small tasks, decide what is most important, and communicate clearly with my manager. I stay calm because panic does not fix bugs.
That is a good habit to build. How is it going so far?
Much better. I now try for thirty minutes, and if I am still stuck, I ask a clear question with what I have already tried.

lines.text: Let us talk about one of your projects. Can you walk me through it?
Sure. It is an expense tracker. Users can add expenses, see monthly totals and filter by category. I built the backend in Java with a REST API and stored the data in a database.
What was the most difficult part?
Handling wrong input. At first the app crashed when someone entered a negative amount. I added validation and returned clear error messages.
How did you test it?
I wrote unit tests for the main logic and tested the API manually with sample data. That helped me find a few bugs before I finished.
Did you work on this project alone, or with others?
Alone, but I asked friends to test it and tell me what was confusing. Their feedback helped me change the screens and the error messages.
Why did you choose Java and a database for it?
Java is the language I know best, and I wanted to learn how real applications store data safely. I used a relational database because expenses have a clear structure.
Can you describe how the data flows when a user adds an expense?
The user sends a request to the API. The controller checks the data and passes it to the service, and the service saves it in the database. Then the API returns a response with the saved expense.
How did you handle errors, for example if the database was not available?
I caught the exception, wrote it in the log, and returned a clear message with the right status code instead of crashing. I also added a retry for a short connection problem.

I would add user login and charts. I would also write more tests, because they make changes much safer.

lines.text: Can you explain the difference between an ArrayList and a LinkedList?

Both store a list of items. An ArrayList uses an array internally, so reading an item by index is very fast. A LinkedList connects items with pointers, so adding or removing in the middle is easier, but reading by index is slow.
Which one would you use most of the time?
Usually an ArrayList, because most programs read data more often than they insert in the middle, and it uses memory more efficiently.
What is the time complexity of searching in a HashMap?
On average it is constant time, order of one, because the key is converted to a hash that points to the right bucket. In the worst case, with many collisions, it can become order of n.
What is the difference between an abstract class and an interface?
An interface describes what a class can do, and a class can implement many interfaces. An abstract class can also hold shared fields and some ready code, but a class can extend only one of them.
When would you choose one over the other?
If I only need a contract, I use an interface. If several classes share common code and state, I use an abstract class. These days I usually start with an interface because it is more flexible.
What is a primary key in a database, and why is it important?
A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table. It cannot be empty or repeated, so other tables can refer to it safely, and the database can find a row quickly.
How would you make a slow query faster?
First I would look at the query plan to see where time is spent. Often adding an index on the column in the where condition helps. I would also select only the columns I need.
Nicely explained. What happens when two keys have the same hash?
That is called a collision. Java stores both entries in the same bucket, in a list or a tree, and compares the keys to find the right one.

lines.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate. What happened?
In a college project, my teammate wanted to finish the work quickly without testing, and I felt it was risky. We both wanted the project to succeed, but we had different ideas.
What did you do?
I listened to his reason first. He was worried about the deadline. Then I showed him two bugs that testing could catch and suggested we test only the most important parts.
And what was the result?
He agreed. We found three bugs early, submitted on time, and the project got good marks. After that we always planned time for testing.
Has there been a situation where you realised you were wrong?
Yes. In another project I insisted on a certain design, but a teammate showed me a simpler approach. I tried it, and he was right. I told him so, and we used his idea.
How do you handle a teammate who is not doing their part?
I would first talk to them privately, without blaming, and ask if they have a problem. Maybe they are stuck or overloaded. If it continues, I would involve our lead.
What if your manager asks for something you think is a bad idea?
I would respect the decision, but I would explain my concern with facts, for example the risk or the extra time. If they still prefer it, I will do it and help make it work.
How do you make sure the team stays friendly after a disagreement?
I keep the discussion about the problem, not the person. Afterwards I thank them for their view, and maybe we have a tea together. Small things help a lot.
What did you learn from that situation?
That it helps to understand the other person's concern first. When people feel heard, it is easier to find a solution together.

items.title: When you do not know the answer

lines.text: How does garbage collection decide which objects to remove?
I do not remember the exact algorithm, but I understand the basic idea. Objects that nothing refers to anymore can be removed to free memory. May I think about it for a moment?
Sure, take your time.

I believe the collector starts from known roots, like local variables, and marks everything reachable. Anything not marked is garbage. I am not fully sure about the details of the different collectors.
That is a good explanation of the basic idea. Would you like to learn more about it?
Yes, definitely. I will read more about it today. It is a topic I want to understand better.
Let us try another one. Can you explain what a deadlock is?
A deadlock happens when two threads each hold a resource and wait for the other to release theirs, so neither can continue. I have only seen it in examples, not in production.
How could you prevent it?
One way is to always acquire locks in the same order. Another way is to use a timeout so that a thread does not wait forever. I am not sure which one is better in every case.
What would you do if you got stuck on a problem like this at work?

I would first search the documentation and the logs, then try a small experiment. If I still cannot solve it after a reasonable time, I would ask a senior colleague with a clear description of what I tried.
Do you prefer to ask for help quickly or struggle alone?
I try to find a balance. I like to try on my own first because I learn more, but I set a time limit so that I do not waste the team's time.
I appreciate your honesty. Let us move to the next question.
Of course. Thank you for explaining.

lines.text: So, are you happy with the offer, or would you like to discuss anything?
I am very excited about the role, and I really want to join. I would like to discuss the salary. Based on my skills and the market, I was expecting something slightly higher.
What number did you have in mind?
I was hoping for something closer to the upper end of the range we discussed, around twelve to thirteen percent above the current offer.
That is a bit above our budget for this role. What if we add a joining bonus?
I appreciate that. A joining bonus helps, but I would prefer an increase in the base salary. Could we find a middle ground, maybe half of what I asked?
Let me ask you honestly: if we cannot change the base salary, would you still join?
I would like to, but I need to think about it. The role is exciting, so I would be open to a smaller increase if there is a salary review after six months.
A six-month review is possible. What else is important for you?
Flexibility in work from home, at least two days a week, and a learning budget for courses. These are very valuable for me.
We have a learning budget of fifty thousand a year, and two days remote is standard.
That is great to hear. With those and a slightly better base, I would be very happy to accept. Could you confirm everything in writing?
Yes, I will update the offer letter and send it by tomorrow.
Thank you very much. I really appreciate your time and flexibility, and I am looking forward to joining the team.
Let me speak to my manager and get back to you tomorrow.
That would be great. Thank you for being open to the discussion.

keys.en: I was expecting something slightly higher
keys.hi: mujhe thoda zyada ki ummeed thi

lines.text: Rahul, you wanted to talk to me. What is on your mind?
Yes, I wanted to tell you in person. I have decided to resign. I have received an offer that is a good step forward for my career.
I am sorry to hear that. Is there anything we can do to change your mind?
Thank you, I really appreciate that. I have thought about it carefully, and my decision is final. I have learned a lot here, and I am grateful for the support.
Okay. What is your notice period?
It is two months according to my contract. I will make sure to complete my current tasks and prepare handover notes for my teammates.
Is there anything specific you would like us to do to make the transition easier?
Yes. I can prepare documentation for my modules and train a teammate during the notice period. I will also finish the tasks that are already in progress.
Who do you suggest should take over your work?
I think Aman would be a good choice because he already knows the payment module. I can start the handover sessions next week if you agree.
Would you be open to leaving earlier if we find a replacement quickly?
Yes, I would be open to that, but I would need to check it with my new company. I will let you know after I speak to them.
Okay. How would you like us to inform the team?
I would prefer that we tell them together, maybe in the team meeting on Monday. I would like them to hear it from me directly, and not through rumours.
Thank you for being professional about it. Please send the formal letter to HR.
I will send it today. I would like to leave on good terms and stay in touch.
Let us talk about your year. How do you feel it went?
I think it went well. I delivered the payment module on time, and I learned a lot about testing. I would like to improve my ability to plan larger tasks.
I agree with that. Your work quality has been good, and the team likes working with you.
Thank you, that means a lot to me. I try to communicate early when there are problems.
One area to work on is speaking up more in meetings.
That is fair feedback. I have been practising my spoken English, and I will try to share my ideas more often.
Do you think the targets we set at the start of the year were fair?
Mostly yes. The only difficulty was that two priorities changed in the middle of the year, so some of my tasks were delayed. It would help to review the targets every quarter.
That is a good suggestion. What was your biggest achievement this year?
Delivering the payment module, because it was my first big responsibility. I also helped two new joiners set up their environment, and I am proud of that.
What kind of support do you need from me to grow?
More chances to present my work to the larger team, and feedback after each release. A mentor for system design would also be very helpful.
I can arrange a mentor. Let us also think about the salary revision.
Thank you. I understand the decision depends on many factors. I would like to know what I can do to be in a strong position for the next review.
Great. Where would you like to grow next year?
I would like to take more ownership, maybe lead a small feature from design to release, and learn more about system design.
Hi Rahul, how can I help you?
Hi, I wanted to ask about the leave policy. How many paid leaves do I get in a year?
You get eighteen paid leaves, and some of them can be carried forward to the next year.
Thank you. And how does work from home work? Is it fixed days or can I request it when needed?
Two days a week are allowed, and you can request more with your manager's approval.
That is helpful. One more thing, how do I claim medical insurance for my parents?
Do you have any other questions about leave or benefits?
Yes. If I work on a weekend because of a release, will I get compensatory leave or extra pay?
You get a compensatory day off, which you must use within two months.
That is fair. And what is the process for reimbursing travel and internet expenses when I work from home?
You upload the bills in the portal by the fifth of the next month, and the amount comes with your salary.
Understood. Also, how can I download my salary slips and tax documents? I will need them for the bank.
They are available in the portal under the payroll section. If something is missing, send me an email.
Perfect. One last thing, who should I contact if I find an error in my salary slip?
You can add them through the HR portal during the enrolment window, which is open until the end of this month.
Great, I will do that today. Thank you for the clear explanation.
Thank you for meeting me, Rahul. This is a short exit conversation. Why did you decide to leave?
Thank you for asking. It was not an easy decision. I got an opportunity with more responsibility and a role closer to my long-term goals.
What did you like most about working here?
The team. People were helpful, and my manager gave me real responsibility early on, which helped me grow.
Is there anything we could do better?
I think a clearer career path and a bit more training on design would help people stay and grow here.
What did you find difficult while working here?
Sometimes the priorities changed quickly, and it was hard to plan. Also, there were not many chances to learn new technologies during working hours.
How was your relationship with your manager?
Very good. He was supportive, gave clear feedback, and trusted me with important tasks. I would work with him again without hesitation.
Do you think the salary and benefits were competitive?
They were fair for the market, but a regular review would help people feel valued. The benefits, like insurance and flexible hours, were very good.
If we offered you a chance to return later, would you consider it?
Yes, I would. I am leaving on good terms, and if the role and the growth are right, I would be happy to consider it in the future.
Thank you, that is useful feedback. Would you recommend this company to a friend?
Yes, I would. I am grateful for everything I learned here, and I hope to stay in touch.

keys.en: it was not an easy decision

lines.text: Hello, thanks for joining. Let me explain what we need. We want customers to book appointments from our website.
Thank you for explaining. To make sure I understand, customers will choose a date and time, and then the system sends a confirmation. Is that right?
Yes, and they should also be able to cancel.
Understood. A few questions: should cancellation be free at any time, or only up to a certain hour before the appointment?
Good point. Free cancellation up to twenty-four hours before.
Perfect. Do you also need email or SMS reminders?
Should customers be able to book more than one appointment at a time?
Good question. Do you want to allow that, or should one customer have only one active booking? It changes how we design the screen and the rules.
One active booking is fine for now, but maybe we will change it later.
Understood. I will build it in a way that is easy to change later. What about payments, do customers pay online when they book, or at the shop?
At the shop for now. Online payment will come in the second phase.
Okay, so no payment in phase one. Who will manage the schedule on your side, and does that person need an admin page?
Yes, one person will manage the slots and see all the bookings.
Great. I will include a simple admin page for that. Let me summarise everything once more, and please correct me if I missed something.
Email is enough for now.
Great. I will prepare a short document with these points and send it today so that we can confirm we are on the same page.

keys.hi: pakka karne ke liye ki main samjha

lines.text: Hi Rahul, how is the project going? Are we on track?
Hello, yes, overall we are on track. The login and booking features are complete and tested, and we are working on the payment page now.
Are there any risks I should know about?
One risk is that the payment provider's test environment has been unstable. If it continues, it may delay testing by a day or two.
What are you doing about it?
We have asked their support team for help, and meanwhile we are building a mock version so that we can continue working without waiting.
How is the team coping with the workload?
The team is doing well. We have four people on the project, and we meet every morning for fifteen minutes to share progress and remove blockers.
Will the budget stay the same?
Yes, as of now we are within the budget. If the payment provider issue continues, we may need two extra days, but I will tell you before we spend any additional time.
Are there any decisions that you need from us this week?
Yes, two things. First, we need the final text for the confirmation email. Second, we need your approval on the colour of the booking button, as the designer has given two options.
I will send both by tomorrow. Anything else?
That is all for now. I will send a short summary of this call by email, with the next steps and the dates, so that we are aligned.
Good thinking. When can I see a demo?
We can show you a working demo next Thursday. I will send an invite today.
Rahul, our customers could not log in for an hour this morning. What happened?
I am very sorry about that, and I understand how serious it is. A change we deployed last night caused the login service to crash.
Is it fixed now?
Yes, we rolled back the change at ten fifteen, and everything has been working normally since then. We are monitoring it closely.
How will you prevent this from happening again?
We will add more testing before each release and a check that stops a faulty deployment automatically. I will share a written report by tomorrow.
Were any customer records lost?
No, no data was lost. The problem was only that the login service was not responding. We checked the database carefully, and all records are safe.
Why did it take an hour to fix?
Honestly, we did not notice it right away, because we had no alert for that service. Once we saw the complaints, it took us fifteen minutes to find the cause and roll back.
What are you doing to find such problems faster?
We are adding an automatic alert that sends a message to the team if the login fails more than a few times in a minute. That will be ready by the end of this week.
Do you think the customers should be informed?
I would suggest a short, honest message from your side, saying that there was a technical issue, that it is fixed, and that no data was affected. I can help you draft it if you like.
Okay, please do that. This is important for us.
Absolutely. Thank you for your patience, and again, I apologise for the trouble.

keys.en: I understand how serious this is
keys.hi: main samajhta hoon ye kitna gambhir hai

lines.text: Hi Rahul, can we set up a call this week to go over the design?
Sure. I am available on Wednesday afternoon or Thursday morning. Which one suits you better?
Thursday morning is good. What time?
How about ten thirty? That would be about thirty minutes.
Ten thirty is fine, but could we make it forty-five minutes? I have a few things to discuss.
No problem. I will send a calendar invite with the meeting link for forty-five minutes.
Who else should join the meeting?
It would be good to have the designer and someone from your side who can approve changes. That way we can decide in the meeting, without waiting for another round of emails.
I will invite our product owner. Should we prepare anything before the call?
Yes, it would help if you could look at the design file in advance and write down your comments. I will send the link and a short agenda today.
Which time zone should we use? We are in different cities.
Let us use Indian Standard Time, and I will also mention the time in your time zone in the invite, so there is no confusion.
Good. Can we record the meeting?
Of course, if everyone agrees. I will start the recording and share the notes and the link after the call.
Thank you. I may need to reschedule if something urgent comes up.
That is perfectly fine. Just let me know a day before if possible.
Hey, are you free for lunch? A few of us are going to the canteen.
Sure, I would love to join. Let me save my work, and I will be there in two minutes.
So, how are you finding the new project?
It is challenging, but I am enjoying it. I am learning a lot, especially from the code reviews.
Nice. Did you watch the match last night?
Yes, it was a great game, especially the last over. I could not sleep for an hour after it.
Which team are you in, again? I do not see you much.
I am in the backend team, on the payments project. Our desks are on the other side of the floor, so I do not come here often.
What do you usually do after work?
Sometimes I go for a walk, and on some days I practise coding or my spoken English. On weekends I like to relax, watch matches and meet friends.
Have you tried the food from the new place around the corner?
Not yet, but I heard it is good. Maybe we can go together on Friday if you are free. I would like to try their thali.
Sounds good. Let us ask the others too.
Yes, let us make a group. It is a good way to know people from other teams.
Same here! Do you play cricket yourself?
Yes, on weekends with friends. You should join us sometime if you like.

keys.hi: mujhe shamil hone mein khushi hogi

lines.text: Hi, I do not think we have met. I am Neha. Are you here for the developer meetup?
Hi Neha, nice to meet you. I am Rahul. Yes, I came to learn about backend development and meet people in the field.
What do you do, Rahul?
I am a Java developer. I mostly work on APIs and databases. How about you?
I work as a tester at a product company. Nice, we should stay in touch.
Definitely. Would you like to connect on LinkedIn? I would like to ask you about testing tools sometime.
What kind of projects are you working on these days?
I am building a small booking application with Java and Spring. I am also learning about testing, so I would love to hear how testers think about quality.
Testing is mostly about thinking like a user and trying to break things.
That is interesting. I think developers often test only the happy path. Do you have any advice for writing code that is easy to test?
Keep functions small and avoid hidden dependencies. Then automated tests become much easier.
That is very useful, thank you. Are there any good communities or groups that you would recommend for a developer who wants to grow?
There is a local Java group that meets monthly. I can add you to the group chat.
That would be great. Thank you for sharing. I am happy I came tonight.
Sure, let me give you my profile name.
Thanks a lot. It was great talking to you, and I hope to see you at the next meetup.

keys.en: It was great talking to you

lines.text: Rahul, today is your last day. We are going to miss you!
Thank you, that is very kind. I am going to miss everyone too. This team has taught me so much.
Where are you going next?
I am joining a product company as a backend engineer. It is a big step for me, and a little scary.
You will do great. Please do not forget us.
Never. Please stay in touch. I will share my number, and we can meet up when I am in town.
What are you going to remember most about this team?
The way everyone helped each other, and the Friday lunches. When I joined, I could barely speak in meetings, and now I can lead a discussion. That is because of all of you.
We will miss your questions in the stand-up!
I will miss them too. Please keep sending me the funny memes, and I will keep sending mine.
Do you have any advice for the new joiners?
Yes. Ask questions early, do not be afraid of making mistakes, and write things down. People here are very kind and happy to help.
That is great advice. Let us take a team photo before you go.
Yes, please. I would like to have one to remember everyone. Let me call the others from the next room.
Definitely. All the best for your new job!
Thank you so much. Take care, and all the best to you as well.

keys.en: We are going to miss you

items.title: Recruiter phone screening
items.hi: Phone par recruiter ka pehla sawaal

lines.text: Hello, may I speak to Rahul, please?
Speaking. Good morning, thank you for calling.
Hi Rahul, this is Neha from a software company. Is this a good time to talk for about fifteen minutes?
Yes, this is a good time. I am in a quiet place, so we can start.
Great. Could you tell me a little about yourself and your experience so far?
Sure. I am a Java developer with a year of project experience. Recently I built an expense tracker with a REST API and a database, and I am now looking for a backend role.
What kind of role are you looking for?
I am looking for a backend developer role where I can work on APIs and databases. I would like a team that does code reviews and supports learning.
Are you open to working from the office, or do you prefer remote?
I am open to a hybrid model. I can work from the office, and I am also comfortable working from home with a good internet connection.
What is your expected salary?
I am looking for a package in line with the market for my experience. I would be happy to discuss the details after I understand the role better.
Do you have any other interviews in progress?
Yes, I have two other conversations, but I am very interested in this position and would like to move forward with it.
That sounds relevant. What is your current notice period?
My notice period is thirty days, and I can discuss an earlier date if needed.

keys.en: I can discuss an earlier date
keys.hi: main jaldi ki date par baat kar sakta hoon

lines.text: Hi Rahul, can you see and hear me clearly?
Yes, I can hear you clearly. The video is fine too. Thank you for having me.
Great. Today I will ask a few questions about Java and your project. Please feel free to think aloud.
Sure, I will explain my thinking as I go.
Can you explain the difference between an ArrayList and a LinkedList?
Of course. An ArrayList uses an array, so reading by index is fast. A LinkedList uses nodes, so inserting in the middle is cheaper, but reading by index is slower.
Which part of the project are you most comfortable explaining?
The backend, especially the REST API and the database design. I can also explain how I handled validation and error messages.
Great. Can you explain how you would design a simple URL shortener?

Sure. Let me think aloud. The user sends a long URL, and the service generates a short code and stores both in a database. When someone opens the short link, the service looks up the code and redirects to the long URL.
How would you generate the short code?
One simple way is to use an auto-incremented id and encode it in base sixty-two. It is short and unique. If we need to hide the sequence, we could add a random part.
What would happen if the traffic becomes very high?
I would add a cache for the popular links, so that the database is not hit each time, and then scale the service horizontally behind a load balancer.
Good. Could you share your screen and show me part of your project?
Sure, let me share my screen. Can you see it now?

keys.hi: main apni screen share karta hoon

keys.en: I will explain my thinking as I go
keys.hi: main saath mein apni soch samjhaunga
main aapko saaf sun sakta hoon

lines.text: So, tell me about your last project and what you.. [the audio breaks up]
Sorry, you are breaking up a little. Could you repeat the last part, please?
Yes, I asked about your last project and what you learned from it.
Thank you. In my last project I built a small booking application, and I learned how to design a clean REST API.
I am sorry, your voice is a bit low on my side.
I think there may be a problem with my microphone. Let me reconnect, one moment.
Is your connection stable now? Should we switch to a phone call?
It looks stable now, but if it breaks again, I can switch to a phone call. May I share my number in the chat as a backup?
Yes, please do that. Let us continue then. Where were we?
You asked about my last project. I built a booking application with a Java backend. The most important thing I learned was how to design clear and consistent API endpoints.
Sorry, can you repeat the last sentence? It froze for a second.
Of course. I said that the most important thing I learned was how to design clear and consistent API endpoints. Is it better now?
Yes, I could hear it now. Thank you for your patience.
No problem at all. Please stop me whenever the audio is not clear, and I will repeat it.
Sure, take your time.
I am back. Can you hear me better now?

keys.hi: kya aap ise dobara bol sakte hain?

items.title: Asking to repeat or clarify
items.hi: Samajh na aaye to dobara poochhna

lines.text: Tell me how you would handle a conflict with a teammate over a technical decision.
Sorry, could you rephrase the question, please? I want to be sure I understand.
Of course. Imagine you and a teammate disagree about the design. What would you do?
Thank you. Let me think about that for a moment.
Take your time.
I would first listen to their reasons, then share mine with an example, and suggest we test both on a small scale. If we still disagree, I would ask our lead for a decision.
Do you want me to repeat anything else before we move on?
Yes, please. Could you speak a little slower? I want to make sure I catch every word, and the line is not very clear.
Of course. Is this speed better?
Yes, that is much better, thank you. I understood the question now: you want to know how I handle disagreement in a technical discussion.
Exactly. Let me ask you a new question. How do you prioritise your tasks?
I list all my tasks and sort them by urgency and impact. If I am not sure what is most important, I ask my lead. Could you give me an example scenario so that I can answer more specifically?
Imagine you have three tasks due today.
Thank you. In that case, I would finish the one that blocks other people first, then the one with the earliest deadline, and I would tell my lead if the third one needs more time.
That is a good approach. Could you speak a little about a time you did this?
Yes. In my college project, we disagreed about the database, so we compared both with a small prototype and chose the faster one.

keys.en: could you speak a little slower?
keys.hi: kya aap thoda dheere bol sakte hain?

keys.en: let me think about that for a moment

keys.hi: kya aap sawaal doosre tareeke se pooch sakte hain?

items.title: Closing the call
items.hi: Call ka end aur agla step

lines.text: Before we finish, do you have any questions for me?
Yes, what does a typical day look like for this role?
You would work in a small team, join a daily stand-up, and build and test features each sprint.
That sounds great. Also, what are the next steps in the process?
We will share your profile with the hiring manager, and you should hear from us within a week.
Thank you. I am very interested in this role, and I look forward to hearing from you.
Is there anything you would like to add that we did not talk about?
Just one thing. I am a quick learner and I take ownership of my work. If I do not know something, I learn it and ask for help early, so there are no surprises.
That is good to hear. What is your availability if we want to schedule the next round?
I am flexible. I can attend an interview any weekday after ten in the morning, and with some notice I can also take a morning slot.
Perfect. Please also keep your resume handy, we may ask for some documents.
Sure. I have my updated resume and my project links ready, and I can send them again by email right after this call.
One more thing, can I confirm your email address?
Yes, it is the same one as in my resume. I will also send you a short message after the call with my details, so that you have everything in one place.
Thank you, Rahul. It was nice speaking with you. Have a good day.
Thank you for your time today. Have a great day!

keys.en: I look forward to hearing from you

lines.text: Hello, this is Priya from the HR team. How can I help you?
Hi ma'am, Rahul this side. Is this a good time to talk?
Yes, I have a few minutes. Which Rahul is this?
Thank you. I applied for the Web Developer opening, and we spoke on the phone the other evening. I wanted to follow up and check if there are any updates regarding the opportunity.
Oh yes, I remember. Let me check the status. One moment, please.
Sure, take your time. I am in no hurry, and I really appreciate your help.
Thank you for waiting. Your profile is with the hiring manager, and he is reviewing a few candidates this week.
Understood. Could you tell me roughly when I can expect to hear back, so that I can plan my time?
We should have a decision by the end of next week.
That is helpful. Is there anything else I can send you in the meantime, like my portfolio, project links or an updated resume?
A link to your portfolio would be great. Please email it to me today.
Of course. I will send it within the hour, with my phone number and email in the signature so that it is easy to find.
Perfect. Anything else you wanted to ask?
Just one thing. If the hiring manager has any questions about my projects, I am happy to explain them on a short call at any time.
Good, I will let him know. We will get back to you soon.
Thank you so much for your time, ma'am. I am very interested in this role, and I look forward to hearing from you. Have a great day!

keys.en: I wanted to follow up on
keys.hi: main ... ke baare mein follow-up karna chahta tha
is mauke ke baare mein koi khabar

items.title: Follow-up after an interview
items.hi: Interview ke baad jawab ka intezaar

lines.text: Hello, Priya speaking.
Good morning, ma'am. This is Rahul. Is this a good time to talk for two minutes?
Hi Rahul. Yes, go ahead.
Thank you. I attended the technical interview for the backend role last Tuesday, and I wanted to check on the next steps. I know these things take time, so I hope I am not disturbing you.
Not at all. We are still discussing a few candidates, so there is no final decision yet.
I understand. Could you tell me whether the interviewer gave any feedback about my interview?
He said your Java basics were strong, but he wanted to see more depth in system design.
Thank you for sharing that, it is really useful. I will work on system design right away. Is there a chance to show that with a small design exercise?
I can ask him. That is a fair request.
I would be grateful. I can do it on a call or as a short written document, whichever is easier for the team.
Okay, I will check and let you know by Friday.
That works well for me. If I do not hear from you by then, may I call you again on Monday?
Yes, that is fine. Call me after eleven.
Thank you, I will do that. I appreciate your time and your honest feedback, ma'am.
You are welcome. Take care, Rahul.
Thank you. Have a wonderful day!

A call is fine. But if I do not pick up, please leave a message.
Understood. Thank you for letting me know, ma'am. I will call you after four.
Okay, talk to you then.
Thank you. Have a good day. Bye!
Hello, Rahul? Sorry I could not take your call earlier.

items.title: Asking for feedback after a rejection
items.hi: Reject hone ke baad feedback maangna

lines.text: Hello, Priya here.
Hi ma'am, this is Rahul. Thank you for your email about the Web Developer role. Is this a good time to talk for a minute?
Yes, sure. How can I help you?
I understand that you decided to move ahead with other candidates, and I respect that. I wanted to ask if you could share some feedback that could help me improve.
Sure. Overall your profile was good. The main gap was experience with React in production.
That is very helpful. Was there any other area where I should improve, such as communication or problem solving?
Your communication was clear. Maybe more practice with real projects would help.
Understood. I will build a larger project with React and deploy it, so that I can show real work next time.
That is a good plan. We also have other openings coming up in a few months.
That is great to hear. May I stay in touch, and can I apply again when a suitable role opens?
Yes, of course. Please keep an eye on our careers page.
I will. Would it be alright if I connect with you on LinkedIn, so that I do not miss any updates?
Sure, send me a request.
Thank you very much for your time and your honest feedback, ma'am. I really appreciate it. Have a great day!

keys.en: share some feedback that could help me improve

main aapke faisle ka samman karta hoon
